Personal project · Automotive engineering

1973 Datsun 240Z Build

A ground-up rebuild of a 1973 Datsun 240Z. The project is a hands-on way to learn across automotive design, mechanical systems, and manufacturing.

Project type
Independent build
Project focus
Ground-up vehicle rebuild
Engineering areas
Automotive · Mechanical · Fabrication
01 / Context

Build objective

The 240Z is a long-running personal engineering project centered on rebuilding a classic car from the ground up. It combines mechanical problem solving with the practical work of planning, making, fitting, and refining vehicle systems.

The project has been part of my hands-on learning in automotive design and manufacturing.

02 / Design process

Work through the systems

The portfolio record will follow the build as a sequence of engineering decisions: inspect the existing system, define the needed repair or change, plan the work, complete it, then check the result.

Build notes will be organized around specific systems and changes so that the reasoning and my own contribution are clear.

03 / Project evidence

Build log structure

  • Starting condition and goals for each system.
  • Design and component decisions, including constraints and trade-offs.
  • Photos, measurements, fabrication notes, or CAD showing the work.
  • Inspection and test results, with follow-up changes where needed.
This is an evolving build. The page will grow with shareable photos and notes from the work, without assigning calendar dates to every update.
